title: Toward a Unified Agentic Security Operations Platform: A Conceptual Architecture for Cross-Domain Cybersecurity Integration
content: Security operations capabilities are commonly distributed across security operations centres (SOCs), security information and event management (SIEM), vulnerability assessment and penetration testing (VAPT), security awareness training (SAT), secure software development life-cycle (SDLC) practices, continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) controls, and AI security testing. Although enterprise platforms increasingly integrate telemetry, detection, response, cloud and identity capabilities, evidence and workflows across these seven capability areas are not necessarily connected through a shared, auditable operating model. This paper proposes a Unified Agentic Security Operations Platform (UASP), a conceptual architecture for coordinating the seven capabilities through specialist agents, a shared telemetry and evidence substrate, risk-context orchestration, and policy-governed human oversight. The framework specifies six illustrative feedback loops, including VAPT findings informing development and pipeline controls, deployment provenance enriching SOC investigations, security incidents informing targeted awareness interventions, and AI security testing events becoming correlated SIEM/SOC telemetry. It distinguishes the operational roles of the SOC and SIEM, and of secure SDLC and CI/CD, while allowing them to be implemented through coordinated agents. The design uses the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) for event normalization and treats entity, temporal and provenance modelling as a complementary semantic layer. It also defines bounded autonomy, risk-graded approvals, and an evaluation agenda. The paper is a narrative conceptual synthesis of selected standards, research and public vendor materials; it does not report a deployed implementation, original empirical dataset, or measured performance results. Its contribution is therefore a structured architecture and a set of testable design propositions for subsequent implementation and evaluation.
